clue.text: Inconvenience of taking foreign currency to Turkish capital

indicators.note: taking one thing to another means attaching it, so the second piece is joined after the first
'capital' keeps only the first letter of 'Turkish'

parts.note: the capital, or first letter, of Turkish
the rouble is the Russian unit of currency

explanation.surface: A traveller grumbles about the hassle of carrying foreign money into Ankara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkish capital' looks like Ankara, but it means only the capital letter of Turkish.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble as a noun is a bother or nuisance, a close synonym for inconvenience.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a songbird with a speckled breast

explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' suggests grumbling, but here it is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a common garden songbird and a yeast infection, a medical complaint.

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
a set is a collection

explanation.surface: An item missing from a collection right from the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: The outset is the very beginning of something, as in 'from the outset'.

clue.text: Coloured girl helpful to the police

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for a noun: the van is something helpful to the police

parts.note: black is a colour
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl assists the police with their enquiries.
explanation.walkthrough: A Black Maria is a police van for carrying prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: Police use the van to transport arrested people, so it is a tool that helps them.

indicators.note: something knocked over lies in a new order, so the letters after it are jumbled

parts.note: the word splits as over plus rate, and only rate is rearranged
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone overvalues the goddess who inspires love poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overrate' looks like one word, but splits into an anagram signal and its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of lyric and love poetry in Greek mythology.

indicators.note: the second word is spread out so that it stretches around the first

parts.note: let means allowed or permitted
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A pet youngster that is always let out to roam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allowed out' reads as one phrase about a pet, but 'out' tells the allowed word to wrap round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a hare in its first year, so it is a young animal.

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A perfume clearance ends with a flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no anagram word; the question mark and 'Dramatic' hint that the letters of the sale must be staged anew.
explanation.definitionFit: The last scene of a play is literally its dramatic ending.

clue.text: The French four returning to vessel

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: la is a French word for the
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's foursome head back to the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A vial is a small bottle, and a vessel is any container for liquid.

clue.text: Band cry at damage to tree

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a verb: to ringbark is to do this damage

parts.note: a ring is a band
a bark is a dog's cry

explanation.surface: A group of musicians shouts at someone vandalising a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, but it is a circular band.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringbarking strips a band of bark right round a trunk, which kills the tree; a common practice in Australian land clearing.

clue.text: Creature that looks wrong with flower

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
a river in France; a flower is something that flows

explanation.surface: An animal looks out of place beside a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword pun for a river, here the Oise in northern France.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortoise is a slow land reptile with a domed shell, one kind of creature.

clue.text: Writer with article on film producer

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows straight after it

parts.note: Philip Roth, the American novelist
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A novelist teams up with a movie producer.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Rotha was a British documentary film producer and director.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Rotha made and produced British documentary films from the 1930s onward.

clue.text: He may not drink with sailor-composer

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
Sir John Stainer, English composer of church music

explanation.surface: A teetotal man keeps company with a seafaring musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sailor-composer' looks like one person, but the hyphen joins two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstainer refuses alcohol, so he is someone who may not drink.

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the normal order, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a house is a dwelling

explanation.surface: Someone rents an odd property to open as an eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: A steakhouse is a restaurant specialising in grilled beef.

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd or out of place, so the letters go into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A river with an odd tidal wave running up it.
explanation.walkthrough: A bore is also a tidal wave up a river, which makes the surface feel watery. The Ebro is the major river of north-east Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ebro is a long river in Spain, flowing to the Mediterranean.

parts.note: ample means roomy or spacious
the Forth, the river of Scotland that flows past Stirling

explanation.surface: A school building sits on a broad river.
explanation.walkthrough: Ampleforth College is a Catholic boarding school in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ampleforth College is a well-known English boarding school run by Benedictine monks.

parts.note: Alfred the Great, King of Wessex
an examiner marks, or grades, a piece of work

explanation.surface: A monarch sits as judge on a stand-up's act.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Marks was a British comic actor and television entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Marks was a well-known British comic performer of stage, radio and television.

clue.text: Spirits raised by short military safari?

indicators.note: short means cut down, so most of the word is lopped off the end
the question mark flags that the words are to be taken loosely and their letters rearranged

parts.note: the first three letters of the word
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Morale gets a lift from a brief army trek through the bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits raised' looks like cheered-up troops, but it means spirits summoned up by a witch.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch's familiar is a demon or spirit she has called up to serve her, often in animal form.

parts.note: surface reading: someone who cannot be relied on
setter's reading: a crossword clue has a surface face and a hidden face, so its compiler deals in double meanings

explanation.walkthrough: The setter teases themself: every clue shows the solver one face and hides another.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deceitful, saying one thing and meaning another, is what makes a person unreliable.

definitions.note: a description of the site rather than a synonym

indicators.note: something discovered has been dug up and turned over, so the letters come out in another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Archaeologists dig up sun-baked mud close to the cathedral city of Salisbury.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Sarum is the abandoned hill-fort site of the original Salisbury, in Wiltshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Sarum is the ancient earthwork and first settlement of Salisbury, two miles north of the present city.

clue.text: Mischievous boy has to inform on patriot

parts.note: Just William, the naughty schoolboy hero of Richmal Crompton's books
to tell on someone is to inform on them

explanation.surface: A naughty lad must report a nationalist to the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: William Brown of the 'Just William' books is the classic mischievous English schoolboy.
explanation.definitionFit: William Tell is the legendary Swiss hero who defied Austrian rule, a national patriot.

clue.text: One in society is quite a limb

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone belonging to a club or association
second meaning: an arm or leg of the body

explanation.walkthrough: 'quite a limb' sounds like describing a wild character, but it only links two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person who belongs to a body such as a society and a limb of the body.

clue.text: Inventor coming up at end of match

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means rising from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the referee's call ending a rugby match

explanation.surface: A famous inventor appears as the final whistle blows.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby, the referee calls 'no side' to end the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison invented the phonograph and a practical electric light bulb.

explanation.walkthrough: Two words that look opposed, speed and immobility, are both meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means quickly, while the adjective means firmly secured, as in a colour that is fast.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a clear run with no rivals in the way
second meaning: a farmer telling workers to empty a paddock

explanation.surface: Nobody objects to the farmer's instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading, an instruction a farmer might give.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a clear field is an idiom for facing no rivals, and a farmer could literally order a field cleared.

clue.text: Care about one kind of nut

indicators.note: about suggests turning round, so the letters are thrown into another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a means one, as in 'a dozen'

explanation.surface: Someone is fussy about a particular nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The areca palm yields the betel nut, chewed widely in South and South-East Asia.

clue.text: In a position to upset island

indicators.note: upset means turned over, and in a down clue that sends the letters back up

parts.note: Elba, Napoleon's island of exile

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to cause trouble on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able to do something means having the means or opportunity, so being in a position to do it.

indicators.note: one word sits in another, so the second goes around the first

parts.note: taken as written, split open to take the other piece

indicators.note: about can mean roughly or turned around, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone muses over the beer stacked in a crate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Think about' reads as one phrase, but only 'Think' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To cerebrate is a formal word for using the brain, that is, to reason or ponder.

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A brain-teaser concerning a car or van.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a picture puzzle where images and letters stand for words.

clue.text: Mother having less trouble with girls

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

indicators.note: to trouble something is to disturb it, so the word's letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A mum finds she has fewer worries with daughters.
explanation.walkthrough: Dam is the usual word for the mother of a horse or other animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsels is an old-fashioned or literary word for young women.

indicators.note: one person getting on after another means following straight behind, so the pieces join in order

parts.note: an ache is a pain
a man's name, short for Ronald

explanation.surface: A man in pain sets off along a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The river here is a mythical one, in the Greek underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Acheron is a river of Hades in Greek myth, crossed by the souls of the dead.
